claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry aged 18–40 years, sampled before and on days 1, 3, and 14 after day-0 influenza vaccination, using linear mixed-effects analysis and regression with the titer response index (TRI), showed that the abundance levels of 494 transcripts were significantly associated with TRI in all subjects.

sources.quote: We found that the abundance level of 494 transcripts signiﬁ- cantly correlated with the TRI (Dataset 8).

claim_3.claim: microarray analysis of whole blood from 92 healthy male volunteers of self-reported Caucasian ancestry aged 18–40 years, before and on days 1, 3, and 14 after day-0 trivalent influenza vaccination, using linear mixed-effects ANOVA and heatmap visualization, showed three distinct patterns of expression for all differentially expressed genes: early upregulation, late upregulation, and downregulation.

sources.quote: A visual summary of the dynamic changes in the transcriptional response to vaccination over time shows three major gene ex- pression patterns: downregulation, early upregulation, and late upregulation (Figure 1A).

Figure 1. The human transcriptional response to trivalent influenza vaccination shows three distinct patterns of gene expression. (A) Heatmap illustrating the patterns of expression for all differentially expressed genes. Yellow indicates a higher value. Three distinct patterns of expression are evident: early upregulation, late upregulation and downregulation.

claim_4.claim: HAI and neutralization assay analysis of serum from 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry ages 18–40 years, before and after day 0 trivalent influenza vaccination, showed that antibody titers measured by hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) and neutralization assays were strongly positively associated.

sources.quote: Antibody titers were measured by both hemagglutination in- hibition (HAI) and neutralization assays. The titer results from these assays were strongly correlated

claim_5.claim: HAI and neutralization assay analysis of serum from 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry ages 18–40 years, before and after day 0 trivalent influenza vaccination, showed that antibody titers generally plateaued after day 14 compared to earlier postvaccination timepoints.

sources.quote: The titer results from these assays were strongly correlated, and the titers generally plateaued after day 14.

claim_6.claim: HAI and neutralization assay analysis of serum from 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry ages 18–40 years, before and after day 0 trivalent influenza vaccination, showed that the Titer Response Index (TRI) scores had a trimodal distribution, facilitating classification of individuals as high, intermediate, and low vaccine responders.

sources.quote: Interestingly, the distribution of the TRI scores is trimodal, facilitating an unbiased classiﬁcation of individuals as high, intermediate, and low vaccine responders (Figure 2A), depending on where the individual’s TRI falls under this dis- tribution.

(A) Probability density estimate of the titer response index (TRI) in our cohort. A trimodal distribution for the vaccine response is observed. The hash marks below the curve are the TRI values for each individual, and the colors correspond to low, intermediate, and high responders.

claim_7.claim: HAI assay analysis of serum from 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry ages 18–40 years, before and after day 0 trivalent influenza vaccination, showed that rise in HAI titer was positively associated with the Titer Response Index (TRI).

sources.quote: The TRI and rise in HAI titer for the 92 individuals show a signiﬁcant positive relationship (r2 5 0.4585).

claim_8.claim: microarray analysis of whole blood from 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry ages 18–40 years, before and on days 1, 3, and 14 after day 0 trivalent influenza vaccination, using regression analysis of gene expression against the Titer Response Index (TRI), showed that the abundance levels of 494 transcripts were significantly associated with TRI.

sources.quote: To assess whether speciﬁc patterns of gene expression correlated with the magnitude of the antibody response, we studied the relationship between gene expression and the TRI in all subjects. We found that the abundance level of 494 transcripts signiﬁ- cantly correlated with the TRI (Dataset 8).

claim_9.claim: microarray analysis of whole blood from 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry ages 18–40 years, before and on days 1, 3, and 14 after day 0 trivalent influenza vaccination, using regression analysis of gene expression against the Titer Response Index (TRI), showed that the 494 transcripts associated with TRI mapped to 481 known genes and 13 nonannotated gene candidates.

sources.quote: We found that the abundance level of 494 transcripts signiﬁ- cantly correlated with the TRI (Dataset 8). These mapped to 481 known genes and 13 nonannotated gene candidates.

claim_10.claim: microarray analysis of whole blood from top 10 and bottom 10 responders among 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry ages 18–40 years, on days 1 and 3 after day 0 trivalent influenza vaccination, using standardized expression values at each time point and averaging of day 1 and day 3 values, showed that residual expression values on days 1 and 3 predicted the observed Titer Response Index (TRI) for each individual.

sources.quote: We then performed a cross-validated linear prediction pro- cedure utilizing the expression values of a subset of differentially expressed genes (Table 1) to predict the antibody response scores of those individuals with the highest and lowest antibody responses as depicted in Figure 2C. We show that the residual expression values on days 1 and 3 are predictive of the observed TRI for each individual

(C) Heatmap of the expression signature of vaccine responsiveness in the top 10 (left) and bottom 10 (right) responders. The expression values for each gene were standardized at each time point, and the day 1 and day 3 values were averaged. Yellow indicates a higher value. Each column represents an individual. The top row illustrates the TRI for each individual.

claim_11.claim: microarray analysis of whole blood from highest and lowest responders among 92 healthy male individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry ages 18–40 years, before and on days 1, 3, and 14 after day 0 trivalent influenza vaccination, using cross-validation prediction, showed that the cross-validated predicted Titer Response Index (TRI) recategorized the highest and lowest responders into the appropriate groups.

sources.quote:
We show that the residual expression values on days 1 and 3 are predictive of the observed

TRI for each individual and, more importantly, that the cross- validated predicted TRI recategorized the highest and lowest responders into the appropriate groups (Figure 2D).
(D) Cross- validation prediction data, illustrating how expression values can be used to predict the TRI.

claim_12.claim: microarray analysis of whole blood from 92 healthy male Caucasian volunteers ages 18–40 years immunized on day 0 with the 2008–2009 trivalent influenza vaccine, sampled before and on days 1, 3, and 14 after immunization, using content analysis, showed enrichment of top pathways including the interferon response and antigen presentation pathways among genes upregulated in the high-responder group compared to the low-responder group.

sources.quote: Content analysis of the genes that were upregulated in the high- responder group showed enrichment of GO categories involved in cellular immune responses, most notably the interferon re- sponse and antigen presentation pathways (Figure 3A and Da- tasets 9, 10).

(A) Top enriched pathways in the high responder group. The negative log P value, along the x-axis, increases as a pathway is more significantly associated. The ratio indicates the proportion of upregulated genes relative to all the genes present in a pathway.

claim_13.claim: microarray analysis of whole blood from 92 healthy male Caucasian volunteers ages 18–40 years immunized on day 0 with the 2008–2009 trivalent influenza vaccine, sampled before and on days 1, 3, and 14 after immunization, showed that interferon pathway genes were preferentially upregulated in the high-responder group compared to the low-responder group.

sources.quote: Genes within the interferon response pathway were highly upregulated in the high-responder group (Figure 3B).
(B) Genes that act in the interferon pathway and which are preferentially upregulated in the high vaccine responders are shown in red.
